docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
mpctrano sits downstream of Trano. The building description (house.yaml) stays the single source of truth: Trano renders it into Modelica models with its FastModel library, mpctrano calibrates them on monitoring data, estimates their state and controls the systems of the building.

 house.yaml ──trano (FastModelMPC)──▶ building_mpc ──rumoca──▶ CasADi ODE  xdot = f(t, x, u, p)
            ──trano (FastModel)─────▶ the same building with the controllers of the YAML (rule-based reference)

docs.title: 1. Model
docs.text:
from mpctrano import FastModel

model = FastModel.from_yaml("house.yaml")                       # calls Trano (FastModelMPC library)
model = FastModel.from_file("house.mo")                         # or the package of `trano create-model house.yaml FastModelMPC`
closed_loop = FastModel.from_yaml("house.yaml", library="FastModel")  # the controllers of the YAML

The FastModelMPC model is close to the Buildings library: layered walls and floors, windows with the angular optics of their glazing, convection and long-wave exchanges in the room, infiltration, the hydronic circuits of the YAML (radiators, valves, mixing valves, pumps, boilers, air-to-water heat pumps and their buffer), ventilation units with heat recovery and PV arrays. The controls of the systems are inputs. FastModel reads everything from the Modelica model:

  • control_names - the inputs with a min and a max: valve positions, mixing valves, boiler part load ratio or heat pump speed (between 0 and 1), the heat of ideal emitters [W];
  • disturbance_names - the weather channels (weather_inputs.TDryBul, .TBlaSky, .winSpe, .winDir, .HDirNor, .HDifHor, .HGloHor) and the internal gains per floor area of each occupancy model (<occupancy>_gai.QRad, .QCon);
  • comfort_states - the air temperature of each zone (<zone>.TAir);
  • meters - the energy the systems drew or produced since the start, states in kWh: EFue (fuel), EEle (electricity of a heat pump), EFan (fans), EPro (PV);
  • simulate(x0, controls, disturbances, dt, start_time) - CVODES simulation, controls held over each step; the model depends on the time of the year (the solar position is computed inside it);
  • with_parameters({...}), select_parameters(patterns), write(directory).

The model is nonlinear and stiff (water nodes): the optimisation problems collocate it on Radau points (trano_optimization), which keeps them stable whatever the step. rumoca does not report the unit of array states (wall layers, radiator water): FastModel restores the kelvin on them so that the collocation scales and bounds them as temperatures.

The variables are named after the elements of the YAML (space_001.TAir, boiler_001.EEle, externalwall_0.G[1]): FastModel.from_yaml generates the model without the containers Trano groups the elements in since 0.57 (network.model(include_container=False)), and FastModel.from_file strips their prefixes (envelope1., production1., ...) from a containerised model, as written by trano create-model. Both give the same model; tests/test_trano_contract.py checks it, with the translation of Trano's models by rumoca, against the installed Trano.

The CasADi export of these models needs rumoca 0.10.3 (rumoca main up to commit c74cddf); uv sync builds it from source, see the installation section of the README. The collocation, the moving horizon estimation and the CasADi model come from trano-optimization (formerly trano.optimization).

docs.title: 2. Disturbances
docs.text: WeatherForecaster.from_model(model) reads the TMY3 .mos weather file of the runnable model (a file of the same name next to the YAML) and the occupancy schedules of the YAML: the weather channels at the middle of each step, the black-body sky temperature computed as the Buildings weather reader does (from the dew point and the opaque sky cover), and the radiant and convective gains of each occupancy model. ForecastNoise adds lead-time dependent errors to the temperatures, the irradiance and the gains; DataForecaster replays recorded disturbances.

docs.title: 3. Calibration, estimation, control
docs.text: See monitoring data, calibration, estimation and MPC.

docs.title: 4. Closed loop, scenarios and the rule-based reference
docs.text:
run_closed_loop(controller, estimator, plant, forecaster, steps) runs the cycle measure → correct → forecast → solve → apply → predict against a ModelPlant (a FastModel playing the real building, with sensor noise) and returns a ClosedLoopResult with the trajectories and the ControlMetrics, read from the meters of the plant: fuel and electricity bought and sold, cost at the price of each carrier, capacity charge, comfort violation in K·h, peak electric power, share of the energy bought below the median price.

run_rule_based(closed_loop, forecaster, start, steps, dt, comfort, tariff) simulates the closed-loop FastModel of the same YAML, with the controllers it describes (thermostats on the valves, the boiler or heat pump holding its supply temperature, the mixing valve its set point), costed and assessed the same way: the reference the MPC is compared with.

Scenario bundles a tariff, a comfort specification, the MPC settings, the forecast noise and the estimator; run_scenario, run_scenario_rule_based and Project.run / Project.run_rule_based execute it; compare puts several runs side by side.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
A FastModel has hundreds of parameters, most of them settled by the YAML (areas, orientations, the optical fits of the glazing) or not identifiable from a few air temperatures. Calibrator adjusts groups of parameters instead, each by one decision variable:

Group Parameters Mode, range envelope_conductance conductances of the wall, floor and roof layers (G[i]), of the glazing gaps and frames factor 0.25-4 envelope_capacity capacities of the layers (C[i]) and of the panes factor 0.25-4 air_capacity the heat capacity factor of the air of each zone (mSenFac, furniture) factor 1-10 infiltration the air changes per hour of each zone (ACH, 0 in Trano) value 0-3 1/h boiler_efficiency the nominal efficiency of the boilers (from the fuel meter) factor 0.7-1.1

OPTIONAL_GROUPS adds the solar transmittance of the windows and the capacity of the radiators, which the air temperatures hardly identify on their own. A ParameterGroup is a set of regular expressions on the parameter names, a mode (scale: the Trano values times a common factor; value: one common value) and bounds; only the parameters the equations depend on are adjusted (the conductances and capacities trano computed from the layers, not the layer data). The heat output of the radiators and the performance maps of the heat pumps are settled when rumoca translates the model and cannot be calibrated.

from mpctrano import Calibrator, CalibrationSettings

calibrator = Calibrator(model, CalibrationSettings(temperature_std=0.1, meter_std=0.05))
calibrated, result = calibrator.fit(training, validation)
result.factors       # the value of each group
result.metrics()     # RMSE and MAE of the air temperatures, training and validation, before and after

The problem is solved with IPOPT on the Radau collocation of the model over the whole period, the parameters symbolic: the states of every step are decision variables bound by the dynamics, so that a long period and poor initial parameters stay well conditioned, and the unmeasured states (walls, water) are free at the start. The objective weighs the errors of the air temperatures (temperature_std), of the energy metered over each step (meter_std) and the deviation of each group from the Trano value (prior_std, regularization). The validation period is simulated from where the training ends.

On the boiler house of the tests, with the conductances x1.3, the capacities x0.8, the air capacity x3, 0.5 air changes per hour and the boiler efficiency x0.9, four days recover x1.35, x0.80, x2.74, 0.47 and x0.904 in about 30 s; the air temperature error falls from 4.5 K to 0.06 K (0.07 K on two validation days). With a single day, the conductances and the infiltration trade with each other: both are losses to the outdoor air.

evaluate(model, data, x0) and simulate_fit(model, data, x0) give the open-loop fit of any model; Project.save() writes the calibration to <stem>.calibration.json and Project.load_calibrated() reads it back.

docs.title: Monitoring data
docs.text:
MonitoringData wraps a regularly sampled, time-indexed DataFrame whose columns are named after the variables of the FastModel:

Column Unit Role time timestamp (first column of the CSV by default) <zone>.TAir K/°C measured air temperature of a zone (at least one zone) valve_001_y.y, boiler_001_y.y, ... - the controls applied, held from each sample to the next boiler_001.EEle, boiler_001.EFue, ... kWh readings of the energy meters, cumulative (optional) weather_inputs.TDryBul, ... K, W/m², m/s, rad the weather channels (optional) occupancy_1_gai.QCon, .QRad W/m² internal gains per floor area (optional; occupancy_1.gai.* before Trano 0.57) 
from mpctrano import MonitoringData

data = MonitoringData.from_csv("monitoring.csv", temperature_unit="C", rename={"Living room": "space_001.TAir"})
report = data.validate(model)              # measured zones, controls, meters, missing columns, gaps
data = data.fill_disturbances(model, forecaster)  # weather file and occupancy schedules for the rest
training, validation = data.split(fraction=0.75)  # the validation starts where the training ends

resample(dt) averages the data on another period, window(start, end) cuts a period, to_csv(path, temperature_unit="C") writes it back.

Without a building at hand, Project.synthetic_data() (or generate_monitoring_data) records data on a copy of the model with its parameter groups at random values (perturb), operated by a thermostat with a random set point that excites the dynamics: the controls, the measured air temperatures with sensor noise, the meter readings and the disturbances.

docs.title: State estimation
docs.text:
The MPC needs the full state of the FastModel (the air, the layers of the walls, the panes, the radiator and buffer water) at the start of each horizon, but only the zone air temperatures are measured. Every estimator follows the cycle correct with the measurement of the step → use the state → predict with the inputs applied during the step (StateEstimator).

MovingHorizonEstimator(model, dt, start, settings=EstimatorSettings(window=12)) keeps the inputs applied and the measurements of the last window steps and, at each correct, finds the trajectory of the model closest to them with the moving horizon estimation of trano_optimization (Radau collocation, IPOPT): the measured air temperatures (measurement_noise), the model errors over each step (process_noise) and the deviation of the first state of the window from its prior (arrival_noise) are weighted by their standard deviations. When the window slides, the estimate of its second state becomes the prior of the next window; when an estimation fails, the prior is propagated over the step instead. Each estimation takes a fraction of a second.

On the boiler house of the tests started 2 K colder than the estimator assumes, the mean error over its 26 temperature states falls from 1.9 K to 0.05 K within a day, where the uncorrected model keeps 0.84 K; the closed-loop MPC with estimation costs the same as with the true state.

PerfectEstimator(plant) returns the true state of a simulated plant, to study the controller alone.

docs.title: Model predictive control, tariffs and flexibility
Optimisation problem
docs.text:
At every step, from the estimated state x0, the time t0 and the forecasts over N steps of dt seconds, ModelPredictiveController solves with IPOPT:

min   Σ_k (π_k b_k − π^in_k (b_k − e_k) + π^fuel_k f_k)    energy cost [EUR], prices in EUR/kWh
    + c_cap · P_peak / 1000                                 capacity charge [EUR/kW] on the peak electric power
    + Σ_k (w₁ (s⁻ + s⁺) + w₂ (s⁻² + s⁺²)) · dt / 3600       comfort violations [K·h]
    + w_lim · Σ_k s_lim,k · dt / 3.6e6                      electricity above a demand response power limit
    + w_move · Σ_k |v_k − v_{k−1}|² + w_effort · Σ_k |v_k|²   moves and effort of the controls (scaled to [0, 1])
s.t.  the FastModel collocated on Radau IIA points in each step
      the bounds of each control (0-1 for the valves, the heat pump speed and the boiler load)
      T_lower,k − s⁻_k ≤ T_zone,k+1 ≤ T_upper,k + s⁺_k        soft comfort band on every zone
      P_k ≤ limit_k + s_lim,k,     P_k ≤ P_peak                electric power bought from the grid

e_k is the net electricity of step k [kWh], read from the meters of the model (the electricity of the heat pumps and fans, the heat of the ideal emitters, minus the PV production), b_k its smooth positive part (bought, the rest is sold at the feed-in price), f_k the fuel the boilers drew and P_k = b_k / dt the electric power. Since the energy comes from the meters, the efficiency of the systems is part of the plan: the COP of a heat pump is better in the mild afternoon than in the cold night, the efficiency of a boiler depends on its load and its water temperature.

MPCSettings holds the horizon, the time step, the penalties, fuel_price and feed_in_price (the tariff price when not given) and the IPOPT options. The problem is built once (casadi.Opti with the time, the forecasts, the prices and the bounds as parameters) and every solve() updates them and warm starts IPOPT from a CVODES simulation of the previous plan shifted by one step, with a small initial barrier parameter (warm_mu_init), which halves the iterations of the receding-horizon solves. If IPOPT does not converge the last iterate is returned with success=False (the closed loop keeps running and counts the failures), and the next solve starts cold.

Comfort bounds apply at the end of each step (the occupied band starting at 7h constrains the temperature reached at 7h); prices apply to the energy of the step. controller.energy gives the electricity bought and net, the fuel and the electric power of each step of the last plan.

On the heat pump house of the tests (27 states), a 24-hour plan with hourly steps solves in 5 to 20 s; the six-zone heat pump house of the Trano test suite (111 states) takes over a minute.

docs.title: Tariffs
docs.text:
Tariff Description FlatTariff one price TimeOfUseTariff peak / off-peak hours, weekends off-peak unless weekend_peak DynamicTariff a price series (from_csv, synthetic_day_ahead), held between samples DemandResponseTariff any tariff + DemandResponseEvents: price multiplier and/or power cap

The tariffs price the electricity; the fuel has its own price (MPCSettings.fuel_price). Every tariff can carry a capacity_charge [EUR/kW] on the peak electric power of the horizon. A DemandResponseEvent power cap applies to the electric power bought from the grid; it is a soft constraint with a high penalty (power_limit_penalty): it is respected unless comfort would collapse.

docs.title: Comfort
docs.text: ComfortSchedule defines occupied/unoccupied bands in °C with the occupied hours; ComfortSpec assigns a schedule per zone (default otherwise) and map("widen", delta) or map("constant") transforms all of them.

docs.title: Flexibility
docs.text:
The flexibility of a building is what the thermal mass and the buffers allow between the bounds: with a cheap night the controller pre-heats and lets the temperature float during the expensive hours; with a capacity charge it spreads the morning boost; during a demand response event it sheds load. The comfort band is the lever: wide_comfort_band in the scenario catalogue raises its upper bound by 2 K.

Costs are only comparable under the same tariff. value_of_flexibility(model, scenario) runs the scenario twice, with the price-aware MPC and with a price-agnostic one (flat price, same comfort band and model), costs both runs with the tariff of the scenario and reports the saving, the energy shifted and the share of energy bought at low prices.

The reference of a building is its own control: run_rule_based (or Project.run_rule_based) simulates the controllers of the YAML on the same building. On the boiler house of the tests, over a January day with the band of its thermostat, the MPC costs 12 % less than the controllers of the YAML under a flat and under a time-of-use tariff, with almost no discomfort (0.05 K·h against 3.7 K·h, the warm-up of the thermostat), and buys 30 % of its energy off-peak against 10 %.

The controller can only exploit the storage it believes in: with the uncalibrated Trano parameters against a different real building, the pre-heating is mis-sized and the comfort band is missed (tutorial 5 shows it). Calibrate before trusting the price response.

compare(runs, baseline="flat") puts several runs side by side (same tariff for the costs to be comparable):

  • total_cost, cost_saving_pct - energy plus capacity cost and the saving against the baseline,
  • energy_kwh, energy_change_pct - pre-heating costs some extra energy,
  • shifted_energy_kwh - energy moved in time against the baseline (half of the L1 distance of the hourly profiles),
  • low_price_share, mean_price - share of the energy bought below the median price, average price paid,
  • comfort_violation_kh, max_violation, peak_power_kw.

price_response(run) gives the energy bought at each price level.
